candidate_1.name: ECFP fingerprints + LightGBM
candidate_1.approach: Extracts Morgan/ECFP molecular fingerprints from SMILES strings using RDKit and trains an ensemble of Gradient Boosted Regression Trees (LightGBM) for each of the 16 quantum chemical properties. This provides a robust, fast-converging baseline that avoids heavy geometric deep learning overhead while effectively mapping structural motifs to electronic spectra.

alternatives_considered: 3D-Aware Graph Neural Networks (SchNet/DimeNet). We weighed building a continuous-filter convolutional network using the raw 3D atomic positions. It was rejected for Candidate 1 because 3D GNNs demand intensive GPU training and hyperparameter tuning, whereas a classical ML baseline allows rapid validation and reliable scaling under tight computational constraints.
constraints: must use the official QM8 data split or a reproducible 80/10/10 random split
must evaluate MAE across all 16 target properties
must handle missing or invalid SMILES gracefully via RDKit sanitization

evaluation_protocol.metric: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) averaged across all 16 QM8 properties

diagnostic_plan: Compute per-target MAE across all 16 properties (CC2, PBE0, PBE0.1, CAM for energies and oscillator strengths), analyze error distribution percentiles, and check error correlation with molecular heavy atom count.
validation_checkpoint: Run a quick pipeline sanity check on 1,000 samples with 50 boosting rounds to ensure feature extraction and multi-target prediction loops execute without error.
budget_split: 20% pipeline setup and baseline validation, 80% model training, hyperparameter tuning, and diagnostic evaluation.

candidate_2_strategy.condition: If LightGBM underperforms significantly on spatial electronic properties (like oscillator strengths) due to lack of explicit 3D geometry awareness.
candidate_2_strategy.hypothesis: A lightweight 3D-aware architecture (such as SchNet or RDKit 3D geometric descriptors combined with an MLP) would capture spatial quantum interactions more faithfully.
